skill: Describe a square numeric matrix by inspecting zeros relative to the main diagonal and choosing the most specific supplied class.
reasoning_steps: Locate the main diagonal; inspect all strictly upper and strictly lower entries.
Zeros below imply upper triangular; zeros above imply lower triangular. Both imply diagonal; use the best description rather than any true superclass.
For a strict triangular result, exhibit a nonzero on the permitted side to exclude diagonal and the opposite orientation.
response_contract: One radio field, selection, with all five labels: Upper triangular matrix, Lower triangular matrix, Diagonal matrix, Identity matrix, Other. Source choice order varies.
difficulty: Easy sources are strict upper/lower 2x2 and 3x3; moderate sources are nonidentity diagonal 3x3. Canonical has zeros on the permitted side and diagonal.
invariants: Square matrix, direct classification, no operations or transformed matrices.
Definitions inspect zeros on an entire side, not a predetermined witness cell.
Best description resolves nesting: nonidentity diagonal precedes triangular.
Keep the five-label radio bank and short explanatory method.
permitted_variations: Upper versus lower orientation, matrix letter, signs and magnitudes, diagonal entries including zero, placement and number of nonzeros on permitted side, 2x2 versus 3x3 within easy workload.
Moderate: diagonal values can vary while excluding identity unless explicitly supported as a conservative prerequisite-based extension.
Witness a21/a12 is incidental: any strictly lower/upper coordinate may carry the sole nonzero.
Bank order is incidental and may vary independently of correctness.
essential_vs_incidental: Square shape and zero-side definitions are essential. A particular letter, size, sign, diagonal, witness coordinate or correct position is incidental. Transposing a strict triangular matrix must swap upper/lower; changing a diagonal value alone must preserve orientation.

source_cases.problem:
How can we best describe the following matrix? 

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$
source_cases.solution:
Notice that $A$ is a matrix for which all entries above the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & {\color{blue}0} & {\color{blue}0} \\ 6 & -1 & {\color{blue}0} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Therefore, it is a lower triangular matrix.

It is not an upper triangular matrix or a diagonal matrix since there is a non-zero element below the diagonal: $a_{21}=6 \neq 0.$
